**Finding submitted: deviation (fallback target).**

- **Responsive locations checked:** § 7 ¶ 10 (NONASSIGNABILITY, p0042) is the sole assignment provision; § 6 termination (p0032–p0033) contains only mutual convenience and breach rights with no change-of-control trigger or re-pricing right; the preamble has no successors-and-assigns language; other "assign" hits concern personnel staffing and IP assignment of Works, not transfer of the Agreement.
- **Why it fails fallback:** the clause is mutual and applies a not-unreasonably-withheld standard (satisfying two fallback elements verbatim), but it requires the other party's consent for *every* assignment, including to a successor in a merger, acquisition or sale of substantially all assets — no M&A carve-out and no notice-only route.
- **Cure:** one surgical insertion of an exception at the front of the existing sentence ("Except for assignment to a successor upon written notice to the other party"), leaving all remaining words verbatim. No change-of-control deletion was needed, and we did not upgrade to preferred wording (affiliate transfers, competitor bar) since the fallback is the acceptable landing zone.
